name: normalize-phone-number
summary: Normalize a phone number to E.164 format and check its digit-count plausibility for its country code.
description: Strips formatting characters (spaces, dashes, parentheses), determines a calling code (from an explicit leading '+' or from the default_country input), and checks the remaining digit count against a fixed table of plausible national-number lengths for a supported set of country calling codes. Returns the E.164-formatted number when plausible. This is NOT a carrier/HLR lookup and does NOT verify the number is actually assigned, active, or reachable -- it is pure format/plausibility validation, deterministic and offline, using a small disclosed table of supported country codes (see SPEC.md), not the full ITU-T numbering plan database. line_type is always "unknown" in this version since distinguishing mobile/landline/VoIP requires carrier data this capability does not have access to. Known, disclosed limitation: does NOT strip domestic trunk prefixes (e.g. the leading '0' in how a UK or German number is normally written for in-country dialing, such as '020 7946 0958') -- when relying on default_country rather than an explicit '+' prefix, the caller must supply the number already in national-significant-number form (no leading trunk digit), or normalization will report digit_count_implausible for an otherwise-valid domestic-format number.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the phone field, in any common formatting (spaces, dashes, parens, optional leading +).

postconditions.description: When valid: true, e164 is a well-formed E.164 string ('+' followed by 1-15 digits) and country_code/national_number are its decomposition.
Never performs a live carrier/HLR/network lookup -- valid: true means format-plausible for the identified country code, not that the number is assigned or reachable.

side_effects.description: Produces one normalization result derived from the provided phone string; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.
